name: trim-coverage
description: Binary-weighted trim-ladder range, resolution, binary weighting and linearity on bandgap_top over the full PVT grid, against README.md's ratified Trim row (issue #14).
claim: README.md 'Target specification (RATIFIED 2026-07-31)' -> row 'Trim': '1-point resistor trim (binary-weighted segments per DR-0001), range >= +/-5%, resolution <= 0.25%/step (>=5 bits equiv.), magnitude only', corner binding 'performed at 27 C'. Substantiates the trim network delivered by design/bandgap_trim.sch -- a 6-bit binary-weighted ladder of 63 identical ppolyf_u unit segments grouped 1/2/4/8/16/32, each group shunted by one metal-option/probe-pad strap RS0..RS5 -- in series with bandgap_core's fixed base R1. Also substantiates the coverage argument in design/bandgap_trim_network.md: that the implemented range absorbs the untrimmed mismatch spread recorded in sim/mc-untrimmed/.

span_mv.description: RATIFIED spec: trim range >= +/-5%. Read against the 1.20 V target that is +/-60 mV either side of the trimmed centre, so the reachable code-0-to-code-63 span must be at least 120 mV. The ratified row binds at 27 C; applying the check at EVERY grid point is strictly stronger, because the ladder's step is PTAT (see lsb_mv) and the span is therefore smallest at -40 C.

lsb_mv.description: Resolution and monotonicity. The RATIFIED cap is 0.25%/step of 1.20 V = 3.00 mV and it binds at 27 C only; the ladder's step is one unit segment's resistance times the PTAT branch current, so it scales roughly 0.77x at -40 C and 1.34x at 125 C. This grid-wide envelope check is therefore 4.2 mV -- the 3.00 mV ratified cap is evaluated against the 27 C rows in the record, where the spec actually binds. min=0.5 mV fails any corner where the LSB collapsed or went negative, i.e. a non-monotonic or broken ladder.

lin_resid_mv.description: Linearity: measured full scale (code 63) minus the superposition of the six measured single-bit-group weights. A non-zero residual would mean the trim is NOT a pure series-resistance magnitude trim -- e.g. the added series resistance shifting the PTAT current, which would make the trim interact with the temperature coefficient and violate the ratified row's 'magnitude only'.

iq_ua.description: Not a spec check -- the Iq claim lives in sim/iq/. This only asserts the loop was in its intended non-degenerate operating state for the last code of the sweep (code 22); a corner that collapsed would otherwise report a meaningless trim curve.

w5_lsb.description: Binary weighting: the MSB group (32 unit segments) must weigh exactly 32 LSBs (1 unit) at every corner. The +/-0.1 LSB window is tight on purpose -- with identical unit segments the ratio is exact by construction and any real deviation would mean the ladder is not what the schematic says it is. An earlier six-different-lengths version of this ladder read 58.6-68.9 instead of 64.0 across this same grid; see design/bandgap_trim.sch's header for why that structure was rejected.

vref_c22.description: Not a spec check -- a sanity window on the code a 1-point trim picks at tt/27 C. The trimmed-accuracy numbers themselves are reported in the record, against the +/-0.5% stretch target, without being used to gate this bench.
